terms.gloss: herself (as object), referring to the subject
terms.grammar: pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number
evidence: Verg. G. 1.389: sōla in siccā sēcum spatiātur harēnā
terms.comment: The same reflexive as for “himself”: sē does not change for a woman. “With herself, by herself” is sēcum, often with sōla.

terms.gloss: herself (for emphasis: she herself, of her own accord)
evidence: Mart. 13.23.2: ipsa merum sēcum portat et ipsa salem
terms.comment: Stresses the woman, or the thing named by a feminine noun: ipsa merum sēcum portat, the fig brings its own wine. As with “himself”, ipsa agrees with the subject or the object, whichever is stressed.

phrases.latin: tum cornīx plēnā pluviam vocat improba vōce et sōla in siccā sēcum spatiātur harēnā
phrases.english: Then the shameless crow calls for rain with full voice and struts alone by herself on the dry sand.

phrases.latin: Chīa senī similis Bacchō, quem Sētia mīsit, ipsa merum sēcum portat et ipsa salem
phrases.english: Chian figs: like old Bacchus, whom Setia sent, she brings her own neat wine with her, and her own salt.

phrases.latin: quae vulpem cum revocāsset, intrītō cibō plēnam lagōnam posuit: huic rōstrum īnserēns satiātur ipsa et torquet convīvam famē. quae cum lagōnae collum frūstrā lamberet, peregrīnam sīc locūtam volucrem accēpimus: sua quisque exempla dēbet aequō animō patī
phrases.english: Inviting the fox in her turn, she set before her a flask full of minced food; thrusting her beak into it, she ate her fill herself and tormented her guest with hunger. When the fox licked the neck of the flask in vain, the bird is said to have spoken thus: “Everyone should bear with good grace the example he has set.”

phrases.latin: amābat enim sēcum praesentiam meam mōre mātrum
phrases.english: For she loved to have me with her, as mothers do.

phrases.latin: ego ipsa sum, inquit, hīc hospita
phrases.english: “I’m only a guest here myself,” she said.

sources: Lewis & Short: sui · Lewis & Short: ipse
